name: David of Wales
otherNames: Devius Aquaticus (in the Life of Paul Aurelian)
knownFor: A British bishop remembered as the founder of the monastery in the valley of Rosina and the preacher at the synod of Brefi, known almost wholly from Lives written centuries after him.
dates: The Welsh annals give his death in the year their editor numbers 601; the Irish annals Hugh Williams quotes give 588. His Lives give the day, Tuesday the first of March, but no year
place: Wales: the valley of Rosina, which the Britons call Hodnant, in Dyfed; the synod of Brefi, at Llanddewibrefi by the Welsh Life

traces: The Latin Life gives his monks a hard rule of work, silence and plain food: they ploughed without oxen, "every one is an ox to himself".
A list of Irish saints, which Williams dates to the 700s, says the second order of Irish saints received the mass from Bishop David and from Gildas and Docus.
Some penitential canons survive in a manuscript under the heading "De libro Davidis", printed by Wasserschleben.
remembered: The Welsh Life gives his last words: "perform the small things which you have heard and seen with me". The Latin Life has "persevere in those things, which ye have learned of me".
Williams: David as he is known is "the creation, probably, of Ricemarcus", written to magnify the see of Saint David's.

uncertain: Almost all that is told of him comes from two Lives written centuries after him. The Latin Life is signed by Ricemarch; Hugh Williams calls him a writer of the eleventh century and quotes a Welsh chronicle giving his death in 1096 as son of Bishop Sulien. W. J. Rees says the Welsh Life is an abridgement of the Latin, and that such Lives were rooted in general truth but written to stir devotion.

His death year. The Welsh annals give the year their editor numbers 601; the Irish annals Williams quotes give 588. W. J. Rees reports Ussher's 554, at the age of 82, and Rice Rees's "short of 566". Wasserschleben gives 544.
His age. The Latin Life says he lived 147 years. Ussher, as Rees reports him, says 82.
His birth. A bracketed entry from later manuscripts of the Welsh annals has him born thirty years after Patrick left Menevia, in a year the editor numbers 458. No other held source gives a year.
His teacher. His Lives name Paulinus. The Life of Illtud makes him one of Illtud's four pupils; Williams notes that the Life of David does not know Illtud as his teacher.
The synod of Brefi. No held source gives a year for it. The miracle of the rising ground is told by both Lives.
